candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XLIV.18. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'Then Judah came near unto him, and said... let thy servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord'. Ephrem reads Judah's offering of himself as substitute for Benjamin as the OT type of Christ's substitutionary atonement: Judah (the tribe of the future Messiah) offers himself FOR another, anticipating the action of his great descendant. Tewahedo Christology preserves this typology as a key OT witness to vicarious atonement.
